exposure: reasons for obstetric admissions to the ICU (hypertensive disorders, obstetric haemorrhage, non-obstetric reasons)
outcome: level and types of interventions (blood transfusion, mechanical ventilation)
patient outcomes (length of stay, maternal death, probability of recovery)
cohort: The study included 291 obstetric patients admitted to the ICU during pregnancy and puerperium from four Finnish university hospitals.
finding: Severity of illness and organ failure scores generally describe obstetric patients as having a good probability of recovery and a short length of stay in the ICU.
mod_finding: The type of delivery was associated with both severity of illness and level of intervention, with those having a vaginal delivery for non-obstetric reasons demonstrating higher severity and intervention levels compared to those admitted for obstetric reasons or who had a caesarean section.
